  data <- read.csv(file_path)
  return(data)

# Story 1: I want to see the month sales (Quanity*Price) by state from Jan 2019 to Jan 2020. 
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
sales$Quantity <- as.numeric(sales$Quantity)
sales$PriceEach <- as.numeric(sales$PriceEach)

# Check if there are any NA values
sum(is.na(sales$Quantity))
sum(is.na(sales$PriceEach))

# Make sure 'Date' is in Date format
sales$Date <- as.Date(sales$Date)

# Create a Month-Year column from Date
sales$Month <- floor_date(sales$Date, unit = "month")

# Calculate total sales per product line
sales$Total_Sales <- sales$Quantity * sales$PriceEach

# Summarize monthly sales by state
monthly_sales_by_state <- sales %>%
  group_by(Month, State) %>%
  summarise(Monthly_Sales = sum(Total_Sales), .groups = 'drop')

# View the summarized data
head(monthly_sales_by_state)

print(monthly_sales_by_state)

library(ggplot2)
# Aggregate sales data by month
monthly_sales <- sales %>%
  mutate(Month = floor_date(Date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(Month, State) %>%
  summarise(Total_Sales = sum(PriceEach * Quantity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = 'drop')

# Check the first few rows
head(monthly_sales)

ggplot(monthly_sales, aes(x = Month, y = Total_Sales, group = State, color = State)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Monthly Sales Trends by State", x = "Month", y = "Total Sales (USD)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

#Conclusion: I can see California (CA), Oregon (OR), and Texas (TX) are top 3 states that has the highest monthly sales.

#Story 2: I want to see the top 5 products are being sold in California by month

# Filter sales data for transactions in California
sales_CA <- sales %>%
  filter(State == "CA")

# Calculate total quantity sold for each product
product_summary_CA <- sales_CA %>%
  group_by(Product) %>%
  summarise(total_quantity = sum(Quantity))

# Select the top 5 products sold in California
top_5_products_CA <- product_summary_CA %>%
  arrange(desc(total_quantity)) %>%
  head(5)

# Print the top 5 products

# Filter sales data for transactions in California
sales_CA <- sales %>%
  filter(State == "CA")

# Group the data by both Month and Product, and calculate total quantity sold
product_summary_CA <- sales_CA %>%
  group_by(Month, Product) %>%
  summarise(total_quantity = sum(Quantity)) %>%
  ungroup()

# For each month, select the top 5 products sold in California
top_5_products_by_month_CA <- product_summary_CA %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  top_n(5, total_quantity) %>%
  arrange(Month, desc(total_quantity))

# Print the top 5 products sold in California by month
print(top_5_products_by_month_CA)

# Story 5: From graph 2,3,4, we can see AAA Batteries (4-pack) is always the products that get highest sales. Now , I want to find top 5 cities in California, Texas and Oregon that sell this item.
library(ggplot2)

# Filter sales data for transactions involving "AAA Batteries (4-pack)"
batteries_data <- sales %>%
  filter(Product == "AAA Batteries (4-pack)")

# Filter the data for transactions in CA, OR, and TX
batteries_data_filtered <- batteries_data %>%
  filter(State %in% c("CA", "OR", "TX"))

# Group the filtered data by state and city, and calculate total quantity sold
city_summary <- batteries_data_filtered %>%
  group_by(State, City) %>%
  summarise(total_quantity = sum(Quantity)) %>%
  ungroup()

# Select the top 5 cities with the highest quantity sold within each state
top_5_cities_by_state <- city_summary %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  top_n(5, total_quantity) %>%
  arrange(State, desc(total_quantity))

# Filter the batteries data to include only the top 5 cities in CA, OR, and TX
batteries_top_5_cities <- batteries_data_filtered %>%
  filter(City %in% top_5_cities_by_state$City)

# Plot the total quantity of "AAA Batteries (4-pack)" sold in the top 5 cities in CA, OR, and TX
ggplot(batteries_top_5_cities, aes(x = City, y = Quantity, fill = City)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "summary", fun = "sum") +
  labs(title = "AAA Batteries (4-pack) Sales in Top 5 Cities (CA, OR, TX)",
       x = "City",
       y = "Total Quantity Sold") +
  facet_wrap(~ State, scales = "free_x") +  # Separate plots for each state
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability.
  
#Conclussion: I can see Austin, Dallas, Los Angeles, Portland and San Francisco are the top 5 that has highest sales of AAA Batteries (4-pack).
